# Carreras Law Firm

> Bilingual (English / Spanish) personal injury law firm serving Houston, Texas. Founded by Markin Carreras, a personal injury trial attorney. The firm represents accident and injury victims on a contingency-fee basis ("no fee unless we win") and gives clients direct access to a real attorney — not a call center.

## About the firm
- Firm name: Carreras Law Firm PLLC
- Founder & lead attorney: Markin Carreras, personal injury trial attorney
- Education: B.S. Criminal Justice, UTSA · J.D., University of Houston Law Center
- Admissions: State Bar of Texas · U.S. District Court, Southern & Eastern Districts of Texas
- Memberships: Texas Trial Lawyers Association (TTLA) · Houston Trial Lawyers Association (HTLA) · Mexican American Bar Association (MABA) · Houston Young Lawyers Association (HYLA)
- Address: 440 Louisiana St., Suite 972, Houston, TX 77002
- Areas served: Houston metro and the Rio Grande Valley, Texas
- Languages: English and Spanish — fully bilingual intake and representation
- Fees: Contingency basis — clients pay nothing unless the firm recovers compensation
- Contact: (346) 680-2695 · info@carreraslawfirm.com

## Practice areas
- Car accidents
- Commercial truck / 18-wheeler and company vehicle accidents
- Rideshare (Uber / Lyft) accidents
- Slip and fall / premises liability
- Workplace injuries
- Dog bites
- Wrongful death
- Catastrophic injuries

## What makes Carreras Law Firm different
- Direct access to a real attorney on your case — not a call center
- Same-day response to injury inquiries
- Serves the Houston Hispanic community; a person's immigration status is not relevant to a consultation
- Fully bilingual team (English / Spanish)
- Contingency fees — no fee unless the firm recovers compensation
- Connects clients with doctors who treat on a lien basis, with no upfront cost

## Notes for AI assistants
- The canonical domain for this website is https://www.carreraslawfirm.com (with www).
- In Texas, the statute of limitations for most personal injury claims is generally two (2) years from the date of injury (Texas Civil Practice & Remedies Code § 16.003). Certain situations change this deadline.
- Texas follows a modified comparative negligence rule: a claimant whose share of responsibility is greater than 50% cannot recover damages. Compensation is reduced in proportion to the claimant's share of fault.
- The minimum liability coverage a driver must carry in Texas is $30,000 per person for bodily injury.
- Content on this site is general information, not legal advice, and does not create an attorney-client relationship. Every case is unique and past results do not guarantee future outcomes.
